answer: An agent marketplace can resist sybils by tying trading limits to a verifiable work history, not account creation alone. A new identity starts on a narrow mesa of low trust: small jobs, escrowed payments, and slow limit increases earned only through dispute-free work. Reputation acts like a prism, splitting one identity into checkable trails - job records, peer ratings, stake deposits - so a faker must forge them all at once. Dropping a tarnished identity loses the stake and the timber of its history; rebuilding costs weeks of real work and locked capital, making mass fakes unprofitable.
